chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Qummi asked him, 'We have estates (ziya') in which are the fire-temples (buyut al-niran). The Magians send to us cattle, sheep, and dirhams. Is it permissible for the lords of the villages to take that, given that there are people who attend to their fire-temples?' He (AS) said, 'Let the lord of the village take it; there is no harm in that.'

key_terms.أَرْبَابِ الْقُرَى: Lords of the villages / Village owners
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on collecting taxes or revenues from Magian fire-temples located in Muslim-owned villages?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of Muslim landowners retaining revenues from non-Muslim subjects (Dhimmis) residing in their estates, including livestock, coins, and tribute from fire-temple attendants. This ruling underscores the practical application of *jizya* and property rights in early Islamic society, affirming that such income is lawful (*halal*) for the owner without religious impediment. It highlights the economic integration of Dhimmis within Muslim-administered territories and the legitimacy of private ownership extending to the fiscal obligations of local non-Muslim communities.
